benchmarks.name: neutral_binary
benchmarks.note: Protocol comparator only; not an empirical base rate.

resolution_rule: Use the official Federal Reserve FOMC statement released for the September 15-16, 2026 meeting. Resolve TRUE if the statement/implementation action raises both the lower and upper bounds of the federal-funds target range by 25 basis points or more relative to the target range in force immediately before the meeting; otherwise resolve FALSE. Score p=0.58 with Brier and log loss and compare against the frozen 0.61 and 0.584 market-implied probability snapshots plus neutral 0.50. A hawkish hold, dissent, projection change, or later intermeeting action does not count as TRUE. Do not update the forecast probability after CPI, PPI, speeches, or market repricing.
rationale: The already-updated v0.2.14 model assigns H003 a 0.38 lead after August payrolls rose 162K with unemployment at 4.1%, reducing the immediate labor-side constraint on a hike.

Renewed weekly oil pressure and previously elevated services price diffusion keep the inflation-risk branch active, while the Fed's recent reaction-function communication has emphasized price stability.

The probability remains slightly below the 61% Reuters market snapshot because wage growth was moderate at 3.1% y/y, participation improved, Governor Waller has articulated a disinflation/hold case, and August CPI has not yet been observed.
This forecast is distinct from P000023: P000023 tests the inflation state; P000027 tests the policy mapping from the full information set to the September decision.
surprising_if: The FOMC holds rates despite first-release August core CPI >=0.3% m/m, resilient labor, and still-elevated energy pressure; that would weaken the model's current H003 policy-reaction mapping.
The FOMC hikes despite first-release August core CPI <=0.1% m/m and a material retreat in energy/policy expectations; that would imply a tighter reaction function than v0.2.14 assumes.
source_notes: Federal Reserve calendar lists the FOMC meeting for September 15-16, 2026, with the statement at 2:00 p.m. ET on September 16.

Reuters Sep. 4 post-payroll coverage reported approximately 61% and, in a separate close snapshot, 58.4% market-implied probabilities of a September hike. The differing snapshots are frozen as separate external comparators.
BLS first August Employment Situation release: payrolls +162K, unemployment 4.1%, average hourly earnings +3.1% y/y.
